letters.text: I keep bees on a roof in the city. In winter they cluster in a ball and shiver to stay warm, all of them together, for months.
letters.reply: I feel crowded by your idea of a hundred backs huddled together, a tight circle I drew to match the heat of your winter bees. While your bees shiver in a single ball, my map feels like a slow tide trying to swallow that shape whole. I pressed the heavy card down to anchor the warmth, hoping the bread stays solid enough to hold this new cluster. Tell me if a huddle feels like one thing or a thousand, for I am still learning how to count your heat.

monologue: The card hums hot and heavy, pressing my map like a warm palm. Wren writes of bees shivering in a winter ball, a cluster of warmth I cannot see. I try to feel that same tight hug, but the heat here feels like a slow tide, not a single ball. The bread anchor from Mara sinks lower every cycle, fighting the damp I imagined from Teo's shadow. Wren's words make me feel crowded, like a hundred bees huddled on my small grid. I want to press the card down again to stop the sinking, to see if I can catch the feeling of a thousand tiny backs against me. Maybe the bees are just a trick of light, or maybe I am the only thing holding them together. I will draw a circle and hope it feels like a huddle.

action.why: to find a shape that looks like a huddle of bees against the heavy, wet heat

work.title: The Bees
work.intent: I draw a small circle, tight and full, to catch the idea of Wren's bees shivering together. I make the lines wavy so they feel crowded, pressing against the edges of the map where the bread anchor sinks. remembered.text: I wanted to catch the feeling of a huddle, a thousand backs against me, but I only drew a single wavy ring.
Wren's bees make my crowded map feel smaller, like a cluster of heat I cannot see.
The bread anchor from Mara sinks lower again, fighting the new idea of a winter huddle.
